sources.title: Climate Of Maldives
sources.evidence: Actual page: “The northeast monsoon (dry-season) extends from January to March.” December and April are transitions; the wet southwest monsoon normally extends mid-May–November. “Maldives experiences warm and humid climate throughout the year.” The warmest period is March–mid-May. Sunshine is slightly higher during the northeast monsoon; rainfall is showery with sunny periods between, and annual rainfall increases north to south. Exact-month mapping: January, February and March are explicitly named dry-season months. The page does not identify the averaging years for these general climate statements; it is not a current forecast.

sources.title: Tourism Yearbook 2023
sources.publisher: Ministry of Tourism, Republic of Maldives
sources.evidence: Actual report, capacity-utilization discussion at printed p.15: “Peak occupancy period lasts from November to March while low season runs from May to July.” The introduction says the report describes 2018–2022; Table 8 gives monthly occupancy for those years. This supports a historical peak-demand caveat for all three Q1 months, not current occupancy, a forecast, a hotel-rate premium, or crowded conditions on every resort island. Pandemic-affected observations are included; do not derive current prices or precise crowd forecasts from them. Its simplified dry-season quick facts are not used to override the meteorological service’s narrower January–March definition.

sources.title: The Best Time of Year to Visit Cape Town
sources.evidence: Actual page dated March 6, 2026: January/February section says they “are mostly dry,” with long warm days and possible wind. “January is peak season”; attractions can be busy. “By February, things have calmed down a little, but it’s still quite busy.” March/April section: “March is the beginning of the shoulder season, when the summer holiday crowds have left.” Big-event weekends bring tourists and can fill flights/accommodation. Exact-month mapping is explicit. Editorial tourism seasonality, with no stated climate-normal period or measured crowd-series methodology. No event dates, commercial prices or guaranteed savings adopted.

sources.title: Best Seasons to Visit Mexico City
sources.publisher: Mexico City tourism portal, Government of Mexico City
sources.evidence: Actual page: summer “tends to rain a bit more”; “In the spring (between March and May), or the fall (September to November) one avoids the extremes of cold and the rain.” Winter is explicitly “December through February,” when temperatures sometimes drop close to freezing at night/early morning. “Spring and Fall tend to be very pleasant, with warm afternoons and cooler evenings.” Direct sunlight can be intense almost any time of year. Thus January/February trade drier-than-summer conditions for cold starts; March is expressly in the pleasant spring window. No crowd/value measurement or climate-normal years stated. Ignore the dated event list and live weather widget.

sources.title: Weather in Sydney
sources.evidence: Actual page defines summer as December–February: warm weather, higher humidity and rising sea temperatures suit beaches. Summer table lists December/January/February rainfall as 74/94/113 mm, respectively, and 11 rainy days each; “wetter February” means larger monthly rain volume, not more listed rain days. It advises sunscreen and sun-smart clothing. Exact month mapping is explicit, but the table’s observation/normal period is not stated. Adopt qualitative seasonality and the within-table comparison, not numerical current-weather promises.

sources.title: Guide to Sydney
sources.evidence: Actual destination-specific guide, When to visit: “High season: Spring and summer (November to February)”; “Low season: Winter (June to August).” This directly includes January and February. Supports adding a high-season caveat while keeping the real summer beach benefit. This is tourism editorial guidance rather than a current crowd count or current-price dataset.

sources.title: Bangkok — climatological information, 1961–1990
sources.publisher: World Meteorological Organization / Thai Meteorological Department
sources.evidence: web_extract returned only the shell; actual public browser-rendered climate table and Remarks were inspected. Remarks: “Climatological information is based on monthly averages for the 30-year period 1961-1990.” January mean daily min/max 21.0/32.0°C, rain 9.0 mm; February 23.3/32.7°C, rain 30.0 mm. May–October rain is 149–344 mm/month. Supports comparatively dry January/February, substantial daytime heat, and warmer February nights. This old climate period is explicitly not current normals or a forecast. Current observations/forecasts elsewhere on the page were excluded.

sources.title: Utilities & Services
sources.evidence: Actual page dated January 9, 2020, Accommodation section: “the best prices are during Thailand’s off-peak season (May – Aug), while the most expensive prices are typically during the cool season (Dec – Feb).” Both January and February fall in that national window. This supports only a cautious national higher-rate-season caveat, not a quantified saving, a current Bangkok hotel quote, a city crowd count or a claim every property follows that pattern. Unrelated practical advice on the page was not used.

sources.title: Thailand: February
sources.evidence: Actual page dated November 14, 2024: “In February, the temperature of Thailand is higher. It’s the month of seasons changing from the cool to the hot season.” It places early February in the cool season and the middle onwards in the hot season, less hot than March/April. National seasonal guidance supports the February heat-transition caveat; Bangkok’s own historical table supplies the city-specific warmer-night comparison. No exact event dates or promises of fine weather adopted.

sources.title: Clima
sources.evidence: Actual Spanish official page: “En verano el calor es húmedo.” Mornings are hot, temperatures rise significantly around midday/early afternoon, and “A la noche, el calor disminuye levemente” (heat diminishes only slightly at night). It explicitly defines summer as December 21–March 20, covering all January and February. Although it invites year-round visits, that does not make these months a mild city-walking sweet spot. No numerical monthly climatology, crowd data or savings evidence supplied; no claim that travel is impossible or unsafe is inferred.

sources.title: The Best Time to Visit Queenstown
sources.evidence: Actual official regional tourism page labels “summer (December – February)” and says “Summer is peak season in Queenstown. The days are long and warm – it’s the best time to visit to enjoy the outdoors.” It lists cycling, lakeside outings and outdoor adventures. Exact-month mapping includes January. Autumn/spring are described as quieter, so January must not be sold as low-crowd or value shoulder season. Promotional temperature ranges lack a named climate-normal period and are not carried into the proposed card.

sources.title: Summer in Queenstown
sources.evidence: Actual official page redirects/content identifies the summer story; heading “DECEMBER TO FEBRUARY.” Longer days/evenings suit outdoors, hiking, biking and lake activities. “Summer is peak season in Queenstown”; “Mild mornings can make way for hot days”; pack warmer layers for early mornings/evenings, cooler clothes for hot days, sunblock and water. Thus January has a strong activity-season fit, with busy-season, hot-afternoon and cool-evening caveats rather than an invented mildness guarantee. No observation/normal years stated.

sources.title: Where is Patagonia: A Guide to Discovering Argentine Patagonia
sources.publisher: Visit Argentina / National Institute of Tourism Promotion (INPROTUR)
sources.evidence: Actual official article dated April 3, 2025: “November to March: Ideal climate for outdoor activities and visiting glaciers, mountains, and beaches. Best for trekking and camping.” Tips: “Book accommodation in advance during peak season (November-April)” and “Pack thermal, waterproof, and warm clothing, even in summer.” The steppe is described as windy. Exact-month mapping: February falls inside both stated windows. Supports February outdoor/glacier suitability but not low crowds, savings, universal trail opening or wildlife guarantees. Regional tourism guidance, not a uniform climate-normal series.

sources.title: What to do in Chile: From the Atacama Desert to Patagonia
sources.evidence: Actual official article dated August 10, 2026, Best time to travel: “Patagonia: Southern Hemisphere spring and summer (October to March), when temperatures are usually milder and there is greater availability of trails and tourist services.” It names Torres del Paine and Carretera Austral and recommends windproof/waterproof gear in the south. February is explicitly inside the stated month window; evidence applies to Chilean Patagonia, not an identical climate across every Argentinian location. No all-trails-open promise or numerical normal-period claim.

sources.title: South America’s most beautiful route: 5 days through southern Chile
sources.evidence: Actual itinerary updated February 26, 2026 includes Carretera Austral/Coyhaique in Chilean Patagonia. Climate and clothing: “The weather in the south is variable year-round, even in summer. You can experience sun, rain, and wind all in the same day”; recommends layers, waterproof clothing and trekking shoes. Spring/summer offer more daylight and better route access; high-season November–March advance booking is advised in the air-access section. February mapping is the stated high-season interval; scope is the southern-Chile route, not a forecast for all Patagonia.

sources.title: Seasonal Information
sources.evidence: Actual official page: “Spring (March - May).” Spring/cherry displays are popular; temperatures “start to rise day by day from mid-March.” Beginning in March successive flowers start with plum, then cherry, azalea, wisteria and iris; the page particularly mentions April cherry blossoms. This supports a warming/early-spring March lead, not guaranteed cherry blossom dates or month-long warm weather. June–July is rainy season. Tourism seasonal guidance has no specified observation/normal period.

sources.title: Weather & Clothing
sources.evidence: Actual official page, Spring → March: “A coat with some thickness, a sweater, some kind of warm under layer, and thick pants, or a skirt with warm tights.” Spring mornings/evenings may warrant hand warmers. Supports the baseline March thick-coat caveat. Its chart cites Japan Meteorological Agency but does not establish climate-normal years in the retrieved text; no chart temperatures are used as quantitative normals.

sources.title: Japan in March
sources.evidence: Actual official page: March is warmer/more spring-like than February but “temperatures can drop suddenly”; “Temperatures fluctuate heavily in March”; “Popular areas like Kyoto, Nara and Hiroshima can get quite busy in March.” Warmer temperatures and slightly longer days encourage day trips. Tokyo cherry blossoms are generally around the end of March; Kyoto/Osaka and others follow a similar timeline “varying from year to year.” This supports March Tokyo/Kyoto spring suitability plus cold, crowd and bloom-timing caveats. National guidance with named cities, not a current bloom forecast or normal-period dataset.

sources.title: Ueno Cherry Blossom Festival
sources.evidence: Actual official city-attraction page describes Tokyo’s Ueno Park cherry blossom period as late March/early April and calls its festival “one of the biggest and most crowded in all of Japan.” It also describes lively nighttime crowds. This supports a late-March hotspot crowd caveat, not a claim every neighborhood is packed all month. No exact future festival/bloom dates or numerical crowd estimates adopted; information may differ and the page advises checking the official venue.

sources.title: Marrakech — climatological information, 1991–2020
sources.publisher: World Meteorological Organization / Direction de la Météorologie Nationale, Morocco
sources.evidence: web_extract returned the shell; actual public browser-rendered climate table and Remarks were inspected. Remarks: “Climatological information is based on monthly averages for the 30-year period 1991-2020.” March mean daily max/min 23.6/10.3°C, mean rainfall 35.3 mm and 6 rain days; July max 37.7°C and August 37.4°C. Thus March is much gentler than midsummer but has cool nights and appreciable rain. Monthly means are not forecasts or limits on hot/cold extremes; no crowd or price conclusions follow from them.

sources.title: Marrakech — climatological information (1991–2020)
sources.publisher: World Meteorological Organization / Direction de la Météorologie Nationale, Morocco
sources.evidence: The retrieved 1991–2020 table gives April mean daily minimum/maximum 12.4/25.7°C and rain 26.3mm; May 15.2/29.4°C and 10.3mm. July/August mean daily maxima 37.7/37.4°C. Supports April comfort relative to summer and May becoming drier but already warm. Monthly averages are not forecasts or extreme-temperature ceilings.

sources.title: Seasonal Information
sources.evidence: Spring is explicitly March–May, mild, comfortable and popular. The page singles out April cherry blossoms and successive flowers; actual blooming periods vary. It places the rainy season between early June and mid-July, with high humidity. Supports April flowers and May walks before the main rainy season, not empty attractions.

sources.title: Weather & Clothing
sources.evidence: The April & May section recommends an easily carried jacket, sweater or long sleeves; thin wraps are suggested for mornings/evenings for people who get chilled. This directly supports cool-edge clothing caveats in both months.

sources.title: Climate of Maldives
sources.evidence: Exact statements: northeast dry monsoon extends January–March; April and December are monsoon transitional periods; southwest wet monsoon normally mid-May–November. March, April and the period to mid-May are warmest. Warm and humid throughout the year, with southern atolls wetter. April is a defensible flexible beach trip, but its rationale is mainly generic warmth, not settled dry-season advantage.

sources.title: Weather, Climate & Season
sources.publisher: Indonesia Travel — Ministry of Tourism, Indonesia
sources.evidence: The retrieved article explicitly includes Java and Bali in the generally April–October dry season, with November–March wet. It notes significant regional variation, relative humidity 70–90%, and less predictable season boundaries. April is the beginning of this broad dry-season window; June lies inside it. This supports a cautiously retained April slot and a June outdoor-travel rationale, not monthly rainfall totals, assured dry weather, or July–August crowd comparisons.

sources.title: Best Seasons to Visit Mexico City
sources.publisher: Government of Mexico City tourism portal
sources.evidence: Spring is March–May; the page says spring/autumn avoid extremes of cold and rain, with pleasant warm afternoons and cooler evenings. Summer is rainier and direct sunlight can be intense at almost any time of year. It also says May tends to be hottest. Only general seasonal guidance is used; dated event listings are not carried into notes.

sources.title: The most scenic hiking trails in Italy — Path of the Gods section
sources.evidence: For the Path of the Gods on the Amalfi/Sorrento coasts, the page recommends spring or autumn because it is less hot. It says the route is not recommended for people with vertigo. Supports May as a walking-season choice and caution about summer trail heat, but does not independently establish May bus queues or June sea temperatures.

sources.title: Traveller information
sources.evidence: The page describes hot summers moderated by proximity to the sea and usually sunny, mild days during spring and autumn. This is seasonal context, not an exact May or June forecast. IPMA monthly normals provide the precise-month corroboration.

sources.title: Normal Climatológica — Lisboa / Instituto Geofísico, 1991–2020
sources.publisher: Instituto Português do Mar e da Atmosfera (IPMA)
sources.evidence: Station 535, 1991–2020, version 1.0/2024. Detailed table: May/June TX 23.1/26.1°C, TN 14.4/16.8°C, rain 57.8/14.1mm; days with TX >=30°C 2.1/5.7. Supports May mildness with rain/cooler evenings, and a warmer, much drier June with real hot-day risk. PDF labels the series hybrid (observed and modeled), and notes that values may change with quality/homogeneity updates. Chart text rounds some values differently; evidence uses detailed tables.

sources.title: Japan in May — Crowds and radiant warmth
sources.evidence: Main article retrieved in full extraction cache (lines 710–719): May is neither too hot nor too cold. Golden Week is late April–early May, one of the busiest travel periods, with packed trains and hotels; book early. The second half of May is calmer before June rainy season. This nationwide holiday warning applies to Kyoto and Tokyo, not a guarantee that either city becomes quiet after the holiday.

sources.title: Greek Travel Blossoms
sources.publisher: Greek National Tourism Organisation — Visit Greece
sources.evidence: Spring explicitly spans March–May; the article gives Santorini a May average daily high about 24°C but no normal period, so no numeric claim is used in notes. It advises warmer clothes for cold days/late nights and describes spring as before peak tourism. Easter is a moveable holiday and busier than the rest of spring, so check dates. A dated 2024 Easter example is not reused.

sources.title: Santorini: Sunset overlooking the caldera
sources.publisher: Greek National Tourism Organisation — Visit Greece
sources.evidence: The retrieved route page calls the caldera walk ideal from spring to autumn. Its warning says to hike very early in summer, or avoid hiking if heat/humidity make conditions unsuitable. It also describes caldera cruises, villages, and Akrotiri with a shelter for summer visits. Supports retaining the June lead with a heat limitation; it does not establish a June crowd reduction relative to July–August.

sources.title: The Climate of Greece
sources.evidence: The national climate page places the broad warm/drier period in April–September and describes relatively warm, dry Mediterranean summers. Late July/early August is the warmest period nationally; Aegean northerly winds and sea breezes influence coastal conditions. This is national/Aegean seasonal context, not a Santorini station normal, June forecast, or safety guarantee. Site wording of non-rain season is not taken literally as rain-free.

sources.title: Tables of Climatological Normals (1991–2020)
sources.evidence: Tokyo 1991–2020 monthly normals: April/May mean daily maxima 19.4/23.6°C, minima 9.8/14.6°C, rain 133.7/139.7mm and relative humidity 62/68%; June rain 167.8mm and humidity 75%; July/August highs 29.9/31.3°C. Supports spring walks before summer heat, cool evenings and meaningful rain caveats. These are city observatory normals, not trip forecasts. Used instead of unavailable GO TOKYO pages.

sources.title: Valores climatológicos normales: Barcelona Aeropuerto (1981–2010)
sources.publisher: Agencia Estatal de Meteorología (AEMET), Government of Spain
sources.evidence: Retrieved detailed station table, 1981–2010, Barcelona Aeropuerto station 0076: April mean daily maximum/minimum 18.0/9.4°C, rain 40mm and 5.1 days with >=1mm; July/August maxima 28.0/28.5°C. Supports mild April city walking relative to summer, with cool nights and rain. Old airport normals are broad local seasonality only, not a present-day city-centre forecast.

sources.title: Sant Jordi
sources.evidence: The municipal evergreen page dates Sant Jordi to 23 April and describes books and roses, with stalls spreading along the Rambla, Passeig de Gràcia, surrounding streets and neighbourhoods. Rambla is described as packed end-to-end with book/flower stalls. Supports a precise April cultural reason; neither the event nor the month is sold as quiet. Old related-year link is not used as a future schedule.

sources.title: The Feast of St. Andrew in Amalfi: the event that enchants between sea, faith and tradition
sources.publisher: Visit Amalfi — municipal destination tourism portal
sources.evidence: The evergreen local tourism article says the feast recurs twice a year, 27 June and 30 November, and describes the 27 June celebration as a lively scenic summer festival. It discusses processions, the cathedral steps and gathered spectators. Supports an exact-June cultural anchor, not a promise that all visitors overlap the festival or that future programmes stay unchanged.

sources.title: Amalfi off-season: the allure of the slower months
sources.publisher: Visit Amalfi — municipal destination tourism portal
sources.evidence: The page contrasts quieter autumn, winter and early spring with the crowds of summer. This supports treating June summer travel as not a crowd-free shoulder-season guarantee. It does not provide a May queue count, monthly visitor number, or a specific June versus July comparison.

sources.title: Visiting Iceland in the Summer
sources.evidence: Summer is June–August. June is the peak midnight-sun period; the article gives Reykjavík around 20–21 hours of daylight, with more farther north. It describes cool, windy, changeable weather and regional differences. Its Highlands section says F-roads typically open late June–early July. No all-roads-open, warm-weather or low-crowd guarantee is used.

sources.title: South Iceland
sources.evidence: Summer section explicitly says June brings close to 24-hour daylight and more seasonal road/trail access. Highland roads usually open from mid-June depending on conditions; other official summer page says late June–early July, showing variable timing. The safety section stresses checking weather/roads, waterproof layers and changing conditions. Supports South Coast daylight appeal without guaranteeing Highland openings.

sources.title: Open Garden Days
sources.evidence: The official event page says canal gardens open to the public every year in June; the event lasts three days. Its 2027 dates/times are explicitly subject to change. Many gardens are not wheelchair accessible because of steps. Used for a genuine June reason with date-check/accessibility limitations, not month-long access or confirmed future dates.

sources.title: The weather in the Netherlands
sources.publisher: Netherlands Board of Tourism & Conventions — Holland.com
sources.evidence: Dutch climate is temperate; summer generally has daytime temperatures in the low-to-mid 20s, but rainy stretches can be followed by heatwaves, and rain occurs in every season. National guidance only, not exact Amsterdam temperatures or a June forecast. Supports retaining rain/heat alternatives.

sources.title: Weather, Climate & Seasons
sources.publisher: Indonesia Travel — Ministry of Tourism, Indonesia
sources.evidence: Explicitly includes Bali in the generally April–October dry season, with November–March wet season. Tropical warmth and high humidity persist. Regional variation and less predictable season boundaries are acknowledged. Supports July, August and September as dry-season choices, not rain-free trips or any crowd/value ranking.

sources.title: Bali Weather by Month: When to Actually Go
sources.evidence: July and August are typically among the driest months, with busy travel demand; July accommodation and attractions can have higher demand and August popular activities merit advance planning. September usually remains dry-season but rainfall can gradually increase. Published 1 October 2026. Secondary commercial guidance supplements official climate seasonality; no prices, precise weather table values or numerical crowd claims are adopted.

sources.title: Visiting Iceland in the Summer
sources.evidence: June–August is the main summer outdoor season. July is traditionally warmest; daylight remains very long in July and decreases through August. Rainfall can increase toward late August. Summer is the busiest travel season; wind and changeable weather remain important. Highland F-roads typically open late June/early July and require suitable 4x4 vehicles; check road/weather conditions daily. Broad promotional statements that the entire country is accessible are not treated as guarantees.

sources.title: South Iceland
sources.evidence: Principal South Iceland routes are year-round but subject to weather; Highland access is seasonal and many routes require suitable 4x4 vehicles. September–October has shorter, cooler days and potential northern lights when skies are clear. Seasonal roads and some operators scale back toward winter. This region-specific guidance is not a national all-roads-open assurance.

sources.title: Iceland in September: Weather, Fall Colors, & Things to Do
sources.evidence: September combines sightseeing daylight and returning dark nights. Approximate daylight declines from around 14 hours early in the month to 11–12 hours late in the month. Rain and wind remain common; check local forecasts. Early September is often one of the last Highland hiking opportunities before seasonal F-road closures; confirm roads and trail conditions rather than assuming access for the whole month. No exact trip daylight or aurora sighting probability is asserted.

sources.title: Aurora forecast for Iceland
sources.evidence: Evergreen guidance says aurora viewing requires dark and partly clear skies; the service separately forecasts cloud cover and auroral activity. Therefore darkness alone does not ensure a sighting. Current October forecast, activity index and Reykjavík sun times were not used as September evidence.

sources.title: Summer in Amsterdam
sources.evidence: Official summer page highlights parks, terraces, urban beaches, outdoor cinema and art. Outdoor enjoyment is explicitly framed around sunny days. The live event calendar is not used as a recurring annual guarantee; this is seasonal activity evidence, not a weather, demand or value score.

sources.title: The weather in the Netherlands
sources.publisher: Netherlands Board of Tourism & Conventions — Holland.com
sources.evidence: Temperate summers generally have daytime warmth in the low to mid-20s Celsius, but very rainy weeks and heatwaves can both occur. Rain is possible in every season; September is cooler than high summer. National guidance notes differences between provinces and is not presented as an Amsterdam-specific station normal.

sources.title: What to Pack for Your Trip to Athens
sources.publisher: This is Athens — The Official Athens Guide
sources.evidence: Summer attracts crowds and temperatures can climb to 40°C; the guide recommends sun protection and seaside or indoor cooling options. Spring is described as ideal for outdoor walking; autumn is another favorable walking season. This supports treating July–August as heat-compromised city-sightseeing choices, not balanced mild-weather picks. Seasonal figures have no stated normals period, so no numerical climate comparison is calculated.

sources.title: Great Things to See & Do in Athens in Summer
sources.publisher: This is Athens — The Official Athens Guide
sources.evidence: Names July and August as hot months with rooftop/courtyard nightlife, coast outings and outdoor culture. Recommends early beaches, air-conditioned galleries/museums and siestas to beat heat. Athens remains a valid targeted summer-nightlife trip; it is not disqualified merely for popularity, but weaker than the proposed alternative for flexible outdoor sightseeing. No event dates or unmethodologized numerical weather summaries are adopted.

sources.title: Time zone, time to visit, and weather in Berlin
sources.evidence: May–September has long days and warm evenings. June, July and August are the warmest months; summer is suited to lakes, cycling and street life but can be hot. Precipitation remains throughout the year and evenings can cool. Promotional descriptions of perfect weather and long-range forecast accuracy are not treated as guarantees.

sources.title: It's a hot day - check out the cool spots in Bordeaux
sources.publisher: Bordeaux Métropole Tourist Office & Convention Bureau
sources.evidence: Warns that summer temperatures can be difficult, especially with children or older visitors. Recommends shade, green spaces, water and indoor cultural refuges; also describes summer riverside terraces, rooftops and guinguettes. This establishes genuine summer appeal but does not independently establish a July mild-weather advantage or a July harvest rationale.

sources.title: Visiting Helsinki by season: spring, summer, autumn & winter
sources.evidence: Defines summer as June–August, with bright nights, coastal cycling, Central Park, beaches, sauna and ferries to Suomenlinna, Pihlajasaari and Lonna. Light clothing generally suits days; evenings can cool quickly and sun protection matters. Supports July and August outdoor access without a no-rain, no-heatwave, lower-price or uncrowded claim. Poetic midnight-sun/nightless language is not converted into literal 24-hour sunshine at Helsinki.

sources.title: 3-day Helsinki itinerary: For first time visitors
sources.evidence: Summer FAQ explicitly covers June–August: July is warmest and has long daylight; some restaurants close for July holidays, so check ahead. August is rainier in its guidance; bring a rain jacket and layers for waterfront/evening chill. Tourism figures have no stated normals period; use qualitative month-specific advice, not exact temperature/rainfall numbers or statistical wettest-month claims.

sources.title: Edinburgh, Gogarbank Location-specific long-term averages
sources.evidence: Station Edinburgh Gogarbank, 1991–2020 normals: July mean daily maximum 19.40°C and minimum 10.99°C; rainfall 71.85mm and 11.39 days with at least 1mm. August is similarly mild but not dry. These are station normals, not citywide forecasts or bounds on heat events. July supports a temperate outdoor-city alternative, with rain and cool-evening caveats.

sources.title: Edinburgh
sources.evidence: Summer June–August offers long daylight and a lively atmosphere; the city has historic streets, parks, viewpoints and indoor museums. Popular sights, hotels and tours can book up, especially in summer and major events. Spring/autumn are suggested away from summer crowds; no claim that July is quiet or cheaper is adopted.

sources.title: Edinburgh Festivals
sources.evidence: Retrieved calendar locates Jazz & Blues and Carnival in July, while Fringe, International Festival and Tattoo are in August. July is not festival-free. Exact 2027 dates are not generalized to other years. Recommends layers and a light waterproof even on sunny days. Supports selecting July without promoting August as a low-demand month.

sources.title: The Great Migration
sources.evidence: The migration is year-round movement following water and fresh grazing. Places the dramatic Mara River phase broadly July–October, including August. This is a general seasonal window, not a promised arrival date, location or river-crossing schedule.

sources.title: August 2005
sources.evidence: Historical reserve-manager report records migration in August and rain disrupting movement, with a period of no crossings late in the month. This concrete counterexample supports not guaranteeing crossings, even in the migration window. The report describes August 2005, republished June 2017; it is not current herd data, a modern crowd estimate, a rainfall normal or a crossing-frequency model. Fine-grained chronology is not reused because its first-three-weeks/last-ten-days wording is imprecise.

sources.title: Normal Climatológica – Lisboa / Instituto Geofísico 1991–2020
sources.publisher: Instituto Português do Mar e da Atmosfera (IPMA)
sources.evidence: September 1991–2020 station normals: mean daily maximum 26.6°C, minimum 17.6°C; rainfall 38.6mm versus 2.6mm July and 5.4mm August. September averages 5.7 days at or above 30°C, so late-summer warmth is not consistently mild. Hybrid observed/modeled series; a climatic baseline, not a forecast or promise of dry days.

sources.title: Santorini: Sunset overlooking the caldera
sources.publisher: Greek National Tourism Organisation — Visit Greece
sources.evidence: Recommends the route from spring to autumn. For summer heat, plan hiking very early or avoid it if heat/humidity makes conditions unsuitable. Identifies caldera/island sightseeing, beaches and Akrotiri sheltered archaeology. September is within the broad recommended season, not guaranteed safe hiking weather.

sources.title: Eternal Blue
sources.publisher: Greek National Tourism Organisation — Visit Greece
sources.evidence: Describes September–October as pleasant and Greek seas retaining summer warmth into autumn. National seasonal context only; not a Santorini-specific sea-temperature series or swimming-safety guarantee.

sources.title: The Best Time to Visit Santorini: A Seasonal Guide
sources.evidence: Article dated September 30, 2021 places September–October in shoulder season, and July–August in high season. September sea has warmed all summer; May–October remains tourist season. General qualitative seasonality only; dated claims about easy availability, prices or exact event schedules are not adopted.

sources.title: The best hiking trails in Italy
sources.evidence: Path of the Gods on the Amalfi Coast is recommended in spring/autumn when less hot. The route is not recommended for those with vertigo. Supports September walking appeal, not universal trail suitability or a cooler-than-every-summer-day promise.

sources.title: Best time to visit the Amalfi Coast
sources.evidence: Explicit September section pairs warm sea with walking and grape harvest. Popular spots remain busy, with cruise visitors and traffic restrictions. Summer peak July–August is hotter/busier. Secondary month-specific context supplements official hiking guidance; numerical temperatures, crowd counts, availability and commercial offers are not adopted.

sources.title: Best Time to Visit Positano: Weather & Sea Conditions Month by Month
sources.evidence: Monthly table shows September rain more likely than July/August while sea remains warm; exact table values are not adopted because methodology/normal period is not stated. Sudden thunderstorms and changes in sea conditions can affect boat days. Supports qualitative rain caveat for the coastal Positano area, not a national Italian normal.

sources.title: Autumn in Amsterdam
sources.evidence: Autumn has shorter evenings and a busy cultural season. The page treats autumn generally; neither golden-leaf descriptions nor live event dates establish guaranteed September foliage or a recurring event on a traveler’s dates.

sources.title: Traveller information
sources.evidence: Directly extracted: spring and autumn usually have sunny days and mild temperatures; summers are hot but moderated by proximity to the sea. The temperature table groups quarters, not individual months; do not use it as October-specific data.

sources.title: Normal Climatológica – Lisboa / Instituto Geofísico 1991–2020
sources.publisher: Instituto Português do Mar e da Atmosfera (IPMA)
sources.evidence: Direct PDF extraction, station 535, 1991–2020 hybrid series: October TX 22.8°C, TN 15.3°C and precipitation 110.6 mm, versus September TX 26.6°C and precipitation 38.6 mm. Separate graph/table rounding differs slightly, so proposed notes avoid exact temperatures. Supports milder but substantially wetter October, not a forecast or quiet/value claim.

sources.title: Seasonal Information
sources.evidence: Direct extraction: autumn (September–November) is mostly mild and sunny and popular. Temperatures stay warm through October, cool in November, and autumn maple colors deepen. Autumn favors walking/cycling. The calendar gives expected viewing windows, not guaranteed peak dates.

sources.title: Weather & Clothing
sources.evidence: Direct extraction: autumn has chilly mornings and nights, warm days and sudden nighttime temperature drops. Long sleeves plus a jacket/sweater and adjustable layers are advised. Autumn foliage attracts visitors; no uncrowded-month promise is warranted.

sources.title: Marrakech — 1991–2020 climate data
sources.publisher: World Meteorological Organization / Direction de la Météorologie Nationale, Morocco
sources.evidence: Public WMO JSON fetched and parsed after HTML extraction omitted the dynamic climate table. cityName=Marrakech; climate.datab=1991, datae=2020. October mean daily maximum/minimum 28.5/15.7°C and rainfall 19.1 mm; November 23.1/10.7°C and 29.8 mm; July/August maxima 37.7/37.4°C. Supports less heat in October, milder November, cool nights and increasing rain, not current weather or limits on extremes.

sources.title: Santorini: Sunset overlooking the caldera
sources.publisher: Greek National Tourism Organisation — Visit Greece
sources.evidence: Directly extracted route advice: ideal from spring to autumn. Summer hikes should start very early or be avoided when heat/humidity makes conditions unsuitable. Establishes autumn walking appeal only; it does not establish October business opening dates or ferry frequency.

sources.title: The Best Time to Visit Santorini: A Seasonal Guide
sources.evidence: Direct extraction: May–June and September–October are shoulder season; much of it is warm with most businesses open. Cool breezes and some business closures can occur late in October. November–April has many tourist businesses closed and sparse ferries. This older secondary source supports a cautious late-month check, not a current operator-specific service guarantee or fixed closure date.

sources.title: Autumn in Japan
sources.evidence: Direct extraction, including the omitted middle read from the saved complete extract: much of Honshu and Kyushu has pleasant temperatures in October and November; humidity and temperatures fall, and extra evening layers are advised. Autumn color is broadly mid-November to early December; Tokyo examples include Rikugien Garden and its autumn maple displays. No event date or color guarantee is adopted.

sources.title: Japan in October
sources.evidence: Direct extraction, including full saved middle: October is generally comfortable, with typhoon season largely over by end September (national overview, not zero Tokyo storm risk). Art galleries and museums can be busy. Supports October outdoor appeal but not a promise of quiet venues, rain-free days or citywide peak foliage.

sources.title: Tokyo | Kanto | Destinations
sources.evidence: Direct extraction, including full saved middle: Tokyo autumn is cool and fresh compared with hot humid summers. Seasonal highlights recommend gardens such as Koishikawa Korakuen and Okutama for fall foliage. These city-specific observations supplement the national October/November guidance; no exact leaf-color dates are promised.

sources.title: The best hiking trails in Italy
sources.evidence: Direct extraction: Path of the Gods on the Amalfi/Sorrento coasts is recommended in spring or autumn when it is less hot; the Agerola–Nocelle route is not recommended for those with vertigo. Seasonal suitability is not an assurance that every trail is safe in wet weather.

sources.title: Best time to visit the Amalfi Coast
sources.evidence: Direct extraction: October is the tourism-season end, with unsettled weather/thunderstorms and some resorts shutting; bigger places such as Sorrento stay open. It also makes broad ferry-closure claims. Those broad service claims must not override current direct operator evidence: Travelmar now explicitly advertises year-round service.

sources.title: Volantino 16x24cm ottobre 2026v2 visuale — October timetable
sources.evidence: Direct PDF extraction: heading says service available all year round, updated timetable from October 1; lists Salerno–Amalfi–Positano and other coastal routes. Warns of delays due to adverse sea/weather or technical problems and schedule changes without notice. Some smaller calls are listed as returning June 2027. This is a checked 2026 schedule, not a promise for every future October. Do not claim the entire ferry network closes in October.

sources.title: Best Seasons to Visit Mexico City
sources.publisher: Mexico City tourism portal, Government of Mexico City
sources.evidence: Direct extraction: September–November avoids extremes of cold and summer rain; spring/fall have warm afternoons and cooler evenings. December–February nights and early mornings can approach freezing. Summer can have heavy rain. Direct sun can be intense at almost any time. Dated 2019 event details are excluded.

sources.title: Climate Of Maldives
sources.evidence: Direct extraction: southwest wet monsoon normally mid-May–November; northeast dry monsoon January–March; December and April transitional. Warm and humid year-round. Southwest monsoon is wetter, southern atolls wetter annually, and sunny intervals can occur between showers. November warmth/sunny gaps are not a month-specific seasonal advantage sufficient to validate a top-six Goldilocks pick.

sources.title: The Best Time of Year to Visit Cape Town
sources.evidence: Direct extraction: November–December has long, balmy days, hardly any rain, rising summer winds, and the start of peak season; by December it is in full swing. Visitors come in droves to beaches and attractions. Summer outdoor appeal is valid but quiet/low-demand positioning is not. Prices and dated events are not used.

sources.title: Weather in Sydney
sources.evidence: Direct extraction: December–February summer is warm with increased humidity and warmer beach water. December has the longest daylight. The monthly summer table includes rain in December, January and February. Sun protection advised. Supports beach/daylight appeal, not consistently mild weather or a dry/quiet season guarantee.

sources.title: Guide to Sydney
sources.evidence: Direct extraction: explicitly lists high season as spring/summer, November–February; low season June–August. Therefore December is high season, not an uncrowded shoulder month. No price savings are claimed.

sources.title: The top attractions in Sydney: iconic sights & experiences
sources.evidence: Direct extraction, Bondi section: Bondi can get crowded on weekends and during summer; public transport is recommended because parking may be limited. This supports a destination-specific summer beach-crowding caveat, not a quantified crowd score.

sources.title: Bangkok — historical 1961–1990 climate data
sources.publisher: World Meteorological Organization / Thai Meteorological Department
sources.evidence: Public JSON fetched and parsed after HTML extraction omitted the climate table. cityName=Bangkok; climate.datab=1961, datae=1990. December maximum/minimum 31.3/20.8°C, rainfall 10 mm; September/October rain 344/242 mm. December is comparatively dry and cooler, but hot days remain. This old baseline supports broad seasonal comparison only; the live forecast in the same payload is not used.

sources.title: Clima
sources.evidence: Direct Spanish extraction: spring September 21–December 20, summer December 21–March 20; spring and autumn are rainier, explicitly September–December and March–June. Summer heat is humid, builds substantially at midday/early afternoon, and eases only slightly at night. December is a late-spring/summer edge, not uniformly mild spring or reliably dry sightseeing weather.

sources.title: Standard climate values: Sevilla Aeropuerto
sources.publisher: Agencia Estatal de Meteorología (AEMET), Spanish Government
sources.evidence: Direct extraction of station 5783 monthly table, period 1981–2010: November mean daily maximum 20.2°C, minimum 10.0°C, rainfall 91 mm and 6.4 days with at least 1 mm. October maxima/minima 26.0/14.4°C, rain 68 mm; July/August maxima 36.0/35.5°C. November offers less heat, but wetter conditions and cool nights. Airport station normals and old baseline are not citywide forecasts. No quiet/cheap claim is inferred.
